body:
> **Now primarily tracked in-repo at `workshop/issues/000002-battle-test-and-scale.md`** — this issue remains as a public-visibility stub per the ariadne in-repo-first convention. The original spec is preserved below.

---

## Goal

Build out factual substrate (`candidates/`, `elections/`, `controversies/`) for as many US jurisdictions as possible by running the algorithm in this repo at scale. Maintainer-paid, AI-curated, all sources cited inline — *not* crowdsourced.

## Phased coverage

### Phase 1 — Battle-test (50 states × top races)
- All 50 states × statewide races (governor, US Senate if year, attorney general, secretary of state, etc.)
- US House for top-N populous districts per state
- Goal: validate the algorithm at multi-state scale; surface state-specific edge cases (e.g., voting systems other than CA top-2 — ranked-choice in ME / AK, partisan primaries elsewhere).

### Phase 2 — Top metros
- Top 50 metro areas × full down-ballot (county / city / school district)
- Where most voters live; highest user-adoption leverage.

### Phase 3 — Full coverage
- All US counties × full down-ballot.
- Aspirational; sets a long-term target.

## Refresh cadence

Per `resolve-ballot.md` cache-invalidation rules tied to proximity-to-election:
- More than 6 months out: refresh monthly
- 2–6 months out: bi-weekly
- 1–2 months out: weekly
- Under 2 weeks out: every few days

Per-cycle full regeneration vs. delta updates: TBD as cost data accumulates.

## AI-transparency requirement (non-negotiable)

Every batch-research run must:
- Use sources from the Tier A/B preference list in `calibration-skills/source-hygiene-tier-list.md`
- Inline source URL for every factual claim (genesis tracking)
- `last-verified` timestamp on every file
- Be reproducible: someone else can clone the repo, re-run the algorithm against the same sources, get equivalent results

## What's needed

- [ ] Batch-research driver: `scripts/populate-jurisdiction.sh` taking `(state, year)` → dispatches research subagents → commits results
- [ ] Makefile target: `make populate-state STATE=CA YEAR=2026` (and variants for county / metro level)
- [ ] Per-state voter-info-tool registry (the equivalent of `smcacre.gov` for each county) so `resolve-ballot` can resolve addresses to districts without per-state custom code
- [ ] CI: validate source-hygiene compliance on every commit (grep for un-sourced claims, weak-source citations, stale `last-verified` dates)
- [ ] Coverage tracking: README table or dedicated `COVERAGE.md` listing which jurisdictions × years are populated and their freshness
- [ ] Cost model: per-jurisdiction AI-bill estimate; budget planning for Phase 1 / 2 / 3 scaling
- [ ] Post-cycle archival: after an election day passes, the manifest becomes historical record — don't delete; document the convention

## Why AI-curated and not crowdsourced?

Wikipedia-style contribution to factual substrate invites bias injection (people adding "facts" they like). AI-curated with consistent methodology + transparent sources sidesteps the whole governance problem.

The pitch to users: *"This is the algorithm. This is the run. These are the sources. Run it yourself to verify — but you don't have to. The bundled version stays maintainer-curated."*

PRs to factual substrate (`candidates/`, `elections/`, `controversies/`) will be closed without merging. PRs to algorithm machinery (`SKILL.md`, sub-skills, templates, `calibration-skills/`, `question-bank.md`) are welcome.

## Initial battle-test (proposed)

Start with what's already populated as a working example:
- CA 2026 cycle: 8 governor candidates + 4 SM County races + 4 CA state races + 1 US House district

Then expand:
1. CA 2026 — fill in remaining CA counties (Phase 1 within one state)
2. Pick 2–3 other large states (TX, NY, FL) for Phase 1 cross-state validation
3. Iterate based on what breaks

- Source repo: https://github.com/xianxu/you-decide
- Development history: xianxu/brain#11 (private)
